provenance.instrument: Borough of Collingdale Zoning Ordinance of 1991 (Chapter 610 Zoning, Ord. No. 589 of 11-9-1992, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 CO2301, Borough of Collingdale, Delaware County (610-31B 'Borough': 'All districts within Collingdale Borough, Delaware County, Pennsylvania'). District use lists and lot, yard and height figures are text in Articles III to V. The chapter has no attachments. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 247. New Laws: Res. No. 2024-25 (police), Ord. No. 199 of 12-30-2024 (Short-Term Rental Ordinance, no chapter named), Ord. No. 2026-01 (rental inspection, sewer laterals) and Ord. No. 2026-02 (tax). None names Chapter 610
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 09-05-2023.' New Laws: four, none naming Chapter 610
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, household employee, conversion, temporary dwelling, apartment addition, habitation, living quarters, caretaker, servant) find in the zoning chapter only the conversion rule (610-28C), the garage rule (610-34C(5)) and the adult use rules

'Rear dwelling. No building to the rear of and on the same lot with a main building shall be erected or used for residence purposes' (610-27B). This holds in every district, so a cottage or other separate unit behind the house is barred

Private garages: rear yard only, at least 3 ft behind the back of the house and 3 ft from every lot line, at most 15 ft tall, and 'Garages shall not be used for permanent or temporary human habitation' (610-34C). A shed may be at most 144 sq ft and 6 ft tall (610-34A)

'Any use not permitted by this chapter shall be deemed to be prohibited' (610-13B). So a second unit added to a house is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (610-50). No bar on a use variance was found

Conversion: the Zoning Hearing Board 'may authorize as a special exception the conversion of any building in an "A" District into a dwelling for not more than three families', if all other A District rules are met, parking follows 610-30, and the yard and building area figures are not reduced (610-28C). The A District asks 5,000 sq ft 'for every dwelling' (610-19B). Whether that counts the converted building once or each unit is not settled

The B Residence District and residential uses in the C Business District permit a two-family semidetached dwelling, including double-duplex dwellings, by right, if the dwelling it shares a party wall with is built at the same time (610-20A(1)(c), 610-22A(1)(a)). Lot area is 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit (610-20B). This is a new twin building, not a unit added to a house. In C a residential use 'shall not be mixed with any other use'

Parking: 2 spaces for a one-family dwelling, 3 for a two-family dwelling and 1.5 per unit for a multiple-family dwelling (610-30D(2)). A fraction up to and including one half is dropped, and a fraction over one half counts as a space (610-30F). Parking may not be in a required front yard, and a driveway must be at least 10 ft wide and reach 20 ft past the front setback (610-30C(2))

Family: any number of people living and cooking together as one housekeeping unit, with no more than two unrelated to the rest. The Zoning Hearing Board may by special exception treat up to three unrelated people as a family (610-17)

Nonconforming lot of single and separate ownership too small or too narrow: buildings may be built or altered only if a special exception is authorized (610-33F). A nonconforming use may be extended by special exception (610-33B)

Floodplain (Chapter 247): a permit is needed for any construction or development anywhere in the borough (247-7). In an AE area without a floodway, 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office' (247-18B(2)(b)). In a floodway no encroachment without a no-rise analysis and no new construction without a DEP permit (247-18A). New construction and substantial improvements of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, and basements are prohibited (247-23A, C(1)). Work costing 50% or more of the building's market value is a substantial improvement (247-34C). Work costing less than 50% 'shall be elevated and/or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible' (247-34E). The zoning chapter gives the Zoning Hearing Board floodplain variances (610-49A(5)), while 247-35 and 247-36 say the Borough of Collingdale grants them. Ask which body hears one

Steep slopes (Chapter 506): 'All freestanding structures, buildings and substantial improvements (with the exception of driveways and utilities when no other location is feasible) are prohibited on slopes of 25% or greater', and on soils mapped as stony land, steep (506-4D). Larger lot areas and lower impervious caps on slopes apply only to lots created by subdivision (506-4A to C)
A 'Duplex' is defined as a detached building with two dwelling units, one above the other (610-17), but no district lists a duplex as a use

In the C District a lot is 75 ft wide with 75 ft of street frontage (610-22C, D). A house in C is 'subject to the requirements of 610-20', so whether the B District widths or the C District widths govern is not settled
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Collingdale Borough Building Official and Zoning Hearing Board. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Read: Chapter 610 Articles I to IX, Chapter 247 Articles I to VII, Chapter 506 (steep slopes), the New Laws page, the table of contents and code searches. Not read: 610-36 (adult uses) and Chapter 247 Article VIII (definitions). Ord. No. 199 (Short-Term Rental Ordinance, 12-30-2024) is a PDF and was not opened. Its search excerpt says a license is needed for each dwelling unit, and that it reaches 'all residential Dwelling Units, conversions of nonresidential structures to residential dwellings'. It reads as a rental licensing ordinance, not a zoning use.
provenance.code_caution: The online code includes legislation through 09-05-2023. Ord. No. 199 (Short-Term Rental Ordinance, 12-30-2024) is not yet in the online code. It names no chapter and reads as a rental license for each dwelling unit, so it may add rules for renting a unit

term.note: Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, household employee, conversion, temporary dwelling, apartment addition, habitation, living quarters, caretaker and servant, and read the use lists of A, B, C, LI-A, LI-B and LI-C. No ADU use

status.note: No district lists a second unit on a house lot, and any use not permitted is prohibited (610-13B). A unit behind the house and a unit in a garage are barred in words (610-27B, 610-34C(5))

status_by_form.note: 'No building to the rear of and on the same lot with a main building shall be erected or used for residence purposes.' Private garages 'shall not be used for permanent or temporary human habitation.'

path.note: A second unit on a house lot is not a permitted use, and any use not permitted is prohibited, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). In the A District a building may instead be converted to up to three units by special exception (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 610-50A(1) to (5). No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion of a building into a dwelling for two or three families (A)
value.conditions: The Zoning Hearing Board 'may authorize as a special exception the conversion of any building in an "A" District into a dwelling for not more than three families', if all other A District rules are met, parking follows 610-30 (3 spaces for a two-family dwelling), and the yard and building area figures are not reduced. The board may set further conditions. The A District asks a lot of 5,000 sq ft for every dwelling, 50 ft wide

disputed_min_lot.note: 610-19B asks 5,000 sq ft 'for every dwelling hereafter erected or used'. 610-28C makes the converted building one dwelling for up to three families, so 5,000 sq ft is the stronger reading. Read as each family's unit, two units need 10,000 sq ft

value.note: A house divided into units, not a unit added to it. The yards and building area may not grow beyond the A District figures

value.name: Two-family semidetached dwelling (B, C)
value.conditions: A two-family semidetached dwelling, including double-duplex dwellings, if the dwelling it shares a party wall with is built at the same time. Lot area 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, 30 ft wide, one side yard of 10 ft. 3 parking spaces for a two-family dwelling. In C a residential use follows 610-20 and 'shall not be mixed with any other use'
value.note: A new twin building with two units in each half, not a unit added to an existing house. The 6,000 sq ft is 3,000 sq ft for each of the two units in one half

historic_bypass.note: No historic district or historic path was found. 610-17 defines a historic building but no rule uses it in the parts read

districts_read_no_listing.note: A, B and C permit dwellings but no second unit on a house lot. LI-A, LI-B and LI-C permit no dwellings

value.condition: In an AE area without a floodway, 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'.

In a floodway no encroachment, new construction or substantial improvement unless an analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction without a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway the rise may be at most one foot. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, and basements are prohibited. Work costing 50% or more of the building's market value is a substantial improvement, and work costing less is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible.

All freestanding structures, buildings and substantial improvements are prohibited on slopes of 25% or greater, except driveways and utilities where no other location is feasible. The same holds on soils mapped as stony land, steep.

types_allowed.note: No ADU use. A unit behind the house and a unit in a garage are barred. A second unit inside a building is only possible through the A District conversion

spaces_required.note: No ADU use. One-family dwellings need 2 spaces and two-family dwellings 3

total_on_site.note: 'Two-family dwellings: 3'. Read for a building converted to two units. A three-unit conversion may be a multiple-family dwelling at 1.5 spaces per unit. A fraction up to one half is dropped and a fraction over one half counts as a space (610-30F)

min_lot_sqft.note: 'A lot area of not less than 5,000 square feet shall be provided for every dwelling', 50 ft wide and 50 ft of street frontage

setback_front_ft.note: On each street the lot abuts

setback_side_ft.note: Two side yards, neither less than 10 ft

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 40% of the area of any lot may be occupied by buildings'

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'A maximum of 2 1/2 stories or 35 feet, whichever is less'

min_lot_sqft.note: Minimum lot area per dwelling unit: single-family detached 3,000 sq ft, 40 ft wide. Semidetached and two-family semidetached 3,000 sq ft per unit, 30 ft wide

setback_side_ft.note: Two side yards, neither less than 10 ft. A semidetached or two-family semidetached dwelling has one side yard

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'A maximum of 2 1/2 stories or 25 feet, whichever is less'

min_lot_sqft_by_type.note: Single-family semidetached: 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, 30 ft wide

min_lot_sqft.note: 'residential uses shall be the same as required in 610-20'. B District uses are permitted in C 'subject to the requirements of 610-20', and a residential use 'shall not be mixed with any other use'

setback_front_ft.note: Read as the B District figure, since a residential use in C is 'subject to the requirements of 610-20'. The C District's own front yard rule (610-22F) is written for business uses

setback_side_ft.note: Read as the B District figure. The C District's own rule asks two 10 ft side yards for a detached building (610-22H)

setback_rear_ft.note: Read as the B District figure. The C District's own rear yard is 10 ft (610-22G)

max_building_coverage.note: Read as the B District figure. The C District allows 85% coverage for its own uses (610-22I)

principal_max_height_ft.note: Read as the B District figure. The C District's own height is three stories or 35 ft (610-22E)

figures_in_dispute.note: The C District sets its own rear yard, coverage and height, and a lot 75 ft wide with 75 ft of frontage (610-22C, D). A residential use in C is 'subject to the requirements of 610-20', so the row shows the B District figures. Which set governs a house in C is not settled
